  agent's reason (untrusted, not part of the approval): "all findings settled in 4 full rounds (max_rounds=4) with cross-family reviewers grok-4.7 (xai) + gemini-3.5-flash-lite (google) + kimi-k3 (moonshot): 2 findings refuted, 0 confirmed, 0 untriaged; review rounds do not converge past already-refuted findings (B-review-delta-rounds-do-not-converge). Q…"

Recover + finish interrupted ddflow item LK-sg-events-followup-tests (P-lock-lifecycle): re-claim salvaged code, finish rubber_duck+critic reviews with grok/x.ai + gemini/google cross-family reviewers, scoped unit_tests before merge, then merge and complete --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813-Godzila --regression-test tests/test_handoff_events.py

chunk_findings.detail: The new unquoted alternative `a/[^\s"]+`/`b/[^\s"]+` cannot match a real `git diff` header whose filename contains a space. `git diff` emits this as unquoted: `diff --git a/foo bar b/foo bar` for a file named `foo bar`. `_FILE.match` returns `None` for that line, so `shape` never appends `foo bar` to `self.files`. A patch whose first file has a space causes all of that file's lines to be skipped while `self.files` is empty, so the too-many-files bound sees fewer files than the patch contains and can be bypassed by under-count.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11 `_FILE`

chunk_findings.detail: A filename containing a double quote is emitted by Git with the quote C-escaped inside a quoted side, e.g. `diff --git "a/foo\"bar" "b/foo\"bar"` for the path `foo"bar`. The quoted alternatives `"a/[^"]*"` and `"b/[^"]*"` stop at that escaped quote byte (`\"` is a literal `"` character in the patch text), so the regex cannot consume the closing quote and `_FILE.match` returns `None`. `_dequote` has a `"` escape specifically to decode `\"`, but the regex never lets such a path reach it; the file is omitted from `self.files`, under-counting the patch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11 `_FILE`

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `not q.malformed` for a patch containing two distinct file paths. That is inverted: this is the exact case where the too-many-files bound the test claims to guard should mark the patch malformed. With the fixed `_dequote`, `q.files` has length 2, so `P.shape(patch).malformed` is True and the assertion fails. The correct expectation is `assert q.malformed`; collapse of `\200`/`\201` to a single `U+FFFD` would incorrectly produce `not q.malformed`, which is the under-count being prevented.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_handoff_events.py:test_distinct_quoted_non_utf8_names_stay_distinct

chunk_findings.detail: `_FILE` only accepts an unquoted side with no whitespace or `"`, or a quoted side with no raw `"` at all. Git’s default `core.quotePath` emits a name containing `"` as `diff --git "a/foo\"bar" "b/foo\"bar"`; `"[^"]*"` stops at the escaped quote, `$` fails, and the header is ignored. `shape` then never appends that path, and because `not self.files` skips later hunks the patch is recorded as zero files and not malformed — so a suggestion of many such files stays under the too-many-files bound (fail-open). The same miss hits `core.quotePath=false` plus a space: `diff --git a/my file.txt b/my file.txt` does not match `[^\s"]+`, so that file is dropped even though the new comment says unquoted names must be counted as literal paths.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/patch.py:11
